final:
-- Overlays the given settings on the defaults mode=fast and level=3.
-- A later duplicate key overrides an earlier one.
-- Output: mode, level, then the other keys in first-appearance order.
-- Note: the third ex line below looks wrong. Under the stated rule,
-- settings(["x", "mode"], ["1", "fast"]) should give ["fast", "3", "1"],
-- since "1" is the value of key "x". It is kept unchanged because the spec is frozen.

settings(keys: List[str], values: List[str]) -> List[str] =
  pre keys.len() == values.len()
  post out.len() >= 2
  ex settings([], []) == ["fast", "3"]
  ex settings(["mode"], ["slow"]) == ["slow", "3"]
  ex settings(["x", "mode"], ["1", "fast"]) == ["fast", "3", "x"]
  ex settings(["mode", "mode"], ["a", "b"]) == ["b", "3"]
  var mode = "fast"
  var level = "3"
  var others_k: List[str] = []
  var others_v: List[str] = []
  for i in range(0, keys.len())
    let k = keys[i]
    let v = values[i]
    if k == "mode"
      mode = v.copy()
    if k == "level"
      level = v.copy()
    if k != "mode"
      if k != "level"
        var found = -1
        for j in range(0, others_k.len())
          if others_k[j] == k
            found = j
        if found < 0
          others_k.append(k.copy())
          others_v.append(v.copy())
        else
          others_v[found] = v.copy()
  var out: List[str] = [mode, level]
  for w in others_v
    out.append(w.copy())
  out

test_settings() =
  assert settings([], []) == ["fast", "3"]
  assert settings(["mode"], ["slow"]) == ["slow", "3"]
  assert settings(["mode", "mode"], ["a", "b"]) == ["b", "3"]
